তারিখ: ১৫ জ্যৈষ্ঠ, ১৪৩১ বঙ্গাব্দ/ ২৯ মে, ২০২৪ খ্রিস্টাব্দ

Customs Act 2023: This notification is issued under the powers granted by the Customs Act 2023. It provides specific duty and tax exemptions for raw materials imported for producing goods against international tenders.
Customs Duty: Customs duty, regulatory duty, value added tax, advance tax, and supplementary duty may be exempted on raw materials imported for production against international tenders, provided specific conditions are met.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is consulted for the issuance of this exemption order and receives audit reports following the supply of goods.
Industrial IRC Holder: To qualify for the exemption, the importing entity must hold an Industrial Import Registration Certificate issued by the Chief Controller of Imports and Exports.
VAT compliant: An importing manufacturer must be VAT compliant, meaning they are registered under the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 and adhere to all accounting, record-keeping, and filing requirements mandated by that law.
Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT: The Commissioner is responsible for approving the input-output coefficients for raw materials and auditing the usage of imported materials after goods are supplied against international tenders.
Consignee: The entity awarded the contract must act as the consignee for all imports and submit relevant documents, including the Notification of Award and contract copies, during the customs clearance process.

Customs Duty Concession: This notification restricts the availability of concessional duty benefits for the import of items described in the schedule.
Imported Goods: The goods listed in the schedule are expressly prohibited from receiving the concessional benefits provided under this notification.

Customs Notification: This notification specifies the date on which its legal provisions come into effect.

Value Added Tax: The certification process requires the declaration of a Value Added Tax registration number for industrial manufacturers seeking to verify the use of imported raw materials for specific contracts.
Industrial Manufacturer: An industrial manufacturer must obtain certification to confirm that imported raw materials, associated with specific letters of credit and invoices, are utilized exclusively for the production of goods under a designated work order.
Raw Materials: The importation of raw materials for production purposes is subject to verification, requiring documentation such as bills of lading, letters of credit, and invoices to match the quantities and descriptions declared for specific contract fulfillment.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the government authority overseeing the submission of specific declarations regarding raw materials and inputs required for production.
Value Added Tax Registration: A formal declaration form requires the submission of a Value Added Tax registration number for the institution applying for the import or use of production inputs.
Customs Commissioner: The declaration form requires the counter-signature of the Commissioner of Customs, Excise and VAT to validate the details regarding production inputs and wastage rates.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: This form serves as a standardized declaration for input-output coefficients, documenting the specific quantities of raw materials and permissible wastage rates involved in manufacturing goods for specific government contracts.

Customs Duty Exemption Schedule: This schedule lists specific categories of industrial and consumer goods that are subject to the provisions outlined in the notification.
The items included in this list range from construction materials and industrial inputs to office equipment and household appliances.
MS Rod or Bar, Angle, and MS Wire: These construction steel items are included as a specific category under the schedule.
Prefabricated Building: Prefabricated building components are identified as a distinct class of goods within this schedule.
Cement: All varieties of cement products are covered under this classification.
Cables: All types of electrical and industrial cables are included in the schedule.
Paint: Paint products are categorized as a specific item subject to the provisions of this schedule.
Fuel and Lubricating Oil: All types of fuel oils, including lubricating oils, are listed as regulated items within this schedule.
Office Equipment and Furniture: All types of office-related equipment and furniture are included in the scope of this schedule.
Air Conditioner: Air conditioning units are explicitly listed as a specific category of goods.
Household Goods: Various categories of household items are included in this schedule for the purpose of the relevant customs regulations.
